extractions.description: An empirical compute-and-simulation study that formulates and evaluates a probabilistic, event-triggered mobility load-balancing procedure for multi-band cellular-network simulations.

type.quote: The experiments are conducted on a proprietary System Level Simulator (SLS) [10]
type.justification: The paper evaluates its proposed procedure through simulator experiments and numerical comparisons, making it empirical.

name.justification: The index terms explicitly identify cellular networks as an application field.

name.quote: Mobility load balancing (MLB) has been recognized as a crucial element of managing radio resources [1], and a core problem in 5G communication networks.
name.justification: The paper proposes and evaluates a new MLB algorithm, directly advancing this field.

name.quote: we model the load balancing problem as a multi-objective stochastic optimization
name.justification: The paper contributes an optimization formulation and transformation for its load-balancing problem.

name.quote: MLB is commonly studied within the context of self-organizing networks (SON)
name.justification: SON is the broader network-management field within which the addressed MLB problem is situated.

name.quote: The experiments are conducted on a proprietary System Level Simulator (SLS) [10], which is a packet-level simulator that emulates traffic for 5G networks based on real-word data.
